  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or

  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">In many domains generating variable length sequences through insertions provides greater flexibility over autoregressive models. However, the action space of insertion models is much larger than that of autoregressive models (ARMs) making the learning challenging. To address this, we incorporate trainable order dynamics into the target rates for discrete flow matching, and show that with suitable choices of parameterizations, joint training of the target order dynamics and the generator is tractable without the need for numerical simulation. As the generative insertion model, we use a variable length masked diffusion model, which generates by inserting and filling mask tokens. On graph traversal tasks for which a locally optimal insertion order is known, we explore the choices of parameterization empirically and demonstrate the trade-offs between flexibility, training stability and generation quality. On <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">De Novo</span> small molecule generation, we find that the learned order dynamics leads to an increase in the number of valid molecules generated, when compared to uniform order dynamics.</p>
  
</div>

The generator network (bottom right) takes in a partial sequence <math id="S0.F1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and produces insertion <math id="S0.F1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> and unmasking <math id="S0.F1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{\theta}\cdot K^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{\theta}\cdot K^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> rates to match the target rates.
</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The dilemma of <span id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">which substructures to generate in what order</span> is highly pronounced for the generative modeling of discrete data.
Autoregressive models generate sequences in a fixed left-to-right order, which is not suitable for many applications where the dependencies in the tokens is are more global <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Valmeekam et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bachmann &amp; Nagarajan, 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dziri et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
In contrast, non-autoregressive models like Masked Diffusion models (MDMs)  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sahoo et al., 2024b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shi et al., 2024</a>)</cite> and Discrete Flow Matching (DFMs) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Campbell et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gat et al., 2024</a>)</cite> learn to generate sequences in arbitrary order.
While this provides flexibility, it also makes the learning difficult <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>.
Specifically, the use of absolute position information and fixed length assumption does not allow the generator to exploit token dependencies that are better expressed in terms of pairwise relative positions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Patel et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
Therefore, learning a good generation order also has limited benefits in the context of fixed length unmasking models like MDMs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To overcome the limitations of fixed length unmasking, several insertion based variable length generative models have been proposed wherein the sequence is generated by inserting tokens  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Havasi et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Patel et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>.
This allows for flexible generation order, while also taking advantage of relative position based token dependencies. However, purely insertion based models forgo the parallel generation benefits of unmasking models.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al. (2025a)</a></cite> proposes FlexMDM, a variable length masked DFM, which combines the benefits of insertion and unmasking based models. FlexMDM unmasks existing tokens and simultaneously inserts new mask tokens in an interleaved manner.
However, the action space of FlexMDM is much larger than that of MDMs. This added expressivity makes learning challenging.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we leverage the flexibility of the DFM framework <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lipman et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> to inject learnable parameters into the data sample dependent insertion and unmasking rates of FlexMDM, which have the effect of controlling the generation order while still maintaining the same terminal time distribution.
By matching those target rates, the generator learns to generate in the order implicit in the target rates.
We show that both the generator and the sample-dependent target rates can be learned simultaneously without the need for simulating the entire trajectory, and in fact using just a single backward pass of automatic differentiation per input sample.
We call our method <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">LFlexMDM</span>, which is short for FlexMDM with <em id="S1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Learnable Order Dynamics</em>.
Experiments on <span id="S1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">de novo</span> molecule generation demonstrate that learned order dynamics lead to significant improvements in the validity and quality of generated samples compared to FlexMDM.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Preliminaries: Discrete Flow Matching</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> be a countable space in which our data lives (e.g., the space of sequences of length <math id="S2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>). The aim is to construct a generative process that samples from a desired distribution <math id="S2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}=p_{\textnormal{data}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>data</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}=p_{\textnormal{data}}</annotation></semantics></math> over this space.
Discrete Flow Matching <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Campbell et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gat et al., 2024</a>)</cite> constructs a continuous time Markov chain <math id="S2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> taking values in <math id="S2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math>, with time marginals <math id="S2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}(x)\coloneqq{\mathbb{P}}(X_{t}=x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}(x)\coloneqq{\mathbb{P}}(X_{t}=x)</annotation></semantics></math>, which transforms an initial sample <math id="S2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{0}\sim p_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{0}\sim p_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> to a final sample <math id="S2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{1}\sim p_{1}=p_{\textnormal{data}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>data</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{1}\sim p_{1}=p_{\textnormal{data}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is easy to sample from.
For small time steps <math id="S2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>, the CTMC transitions follow <math id="S2.p1.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="x_{t+h}\sim p_{t+h|t}(\cdot\mid x_{t})\coloneqq{\mathbb{P}}(X_{t+h}=\cdot|X_{t}=x_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≔</mo><mi>ℙ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{t+h}\sim p_{t+h|t}(\cdot\mid x_{t})\coloneqq{\mathbb{P}}(X_{t+h}=\cdot|X_{t}=x_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>, where the transition probability is given by</p>

<p id="S2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and <math id="S2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{x}(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{x}(y)</annotation></semantics></math> is the indicator function .
The initial distribution <math id="S2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and the rate <math id="S2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> of the CTMC determine the generative process completely. <span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
            
            
            
            
            
            
            
          Please refer to <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Background: Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> for an extended discussion.</span></span></span>
Therefore, to obtain the desired CTMC, one first constructs a <em id="S2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">probability flow</em> <math id="S2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> such that the desired terminal distribution condition is satisfied: <math id="S2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t=1}=p_{\textnormal{data}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>data</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t=1}=p_{\textnormal{data}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and then constructs a (non-unique) generator rate <math id="S2.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> that satisfies the Kolmogorov Forward Equation:</p>

<p id="S2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Such a rate is said to <em id="S2.p1.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">generate</em> the marginal probability path <math id="S2.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The general template is to choose a family of densities <math id="S2.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t|C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo conditioning variable, typically an endpoint pin <math id="S2.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=(X_{0},X_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo encoding="application/x-tex">C=(X_{0},X_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>, and then to match the unknown rates <math id="S2.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\theta}(x,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo the target conditional rates <math id="S2.p1.m23" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="R_{t}(x,\cdot\mid C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(x,\cdot\mid C)</annotation></semantics></math> that generate <math id="S2.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t|C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t|C}</annotation></semantics></math> (in the sense of <a href="#S2.E2" title="In 2 Preliminaries: Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) by minimizing the Bregman divergence:</p>

In the case of <math id="S2.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=(X_{0},X_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=(X_{0},X_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S2.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{1}\sim p_{\textnormal{data}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>data</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{1}\sim p_{\textnormal{data}}</annotation></semantics></math>, this minimizes a lower bound on the data log-likelihood  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shaul et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>

<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Projected DFM:</span> The framework of DFM can be generalized to construct a conditional rate on an auxiliary space <math id="S2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where it may be easier to define the dynamics, and then <em id="S2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">project</em> the rate onto the space of interest <math id="S2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> creating weakly intertwined CTMCs as shown in the schematic in <a href="#S2.F2" title="In 2 Preliminaries: Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.<span id="footnote2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">2</span>
            
            
            
            
            
            
            
          This is a slight generalization of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Havasi et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>. See <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Projected Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a> for the discussion.</span></span></span>
Let <math id="S2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{Z_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{Z_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> be a CTMC taking values in <math id="S2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and define <math id="S2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{enc}}(x\mid z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>enc</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{enc}}(x\mid z)</annotation></semantics></math> to be an <em id="S2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">encoder kernel</em> from <math id="S2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math>, then the auxiliary dynamics induce a (law-dependent) projected CTMC on <math id="S2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> with rate</p>

<p id="S2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z,w\in{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z,w\in{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is the rate for the CTMC <math id="S2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{Z_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{Z_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{dec},t}(z\mid x)\propto p_{t}(z)\pi_{\text{enc}}(x\mid z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mtext>dec</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>enc</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{dec},t}(z\mid x)\propto p_{t}(z)\pi_{\text{enc}}(x\mid z)</annotation></semantics></math> is the Bayes decoder.
The same construction applies to conditional rates <math id="S2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(z,w\mid C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(z,w\mid C)</annotation></semantics></math>, yielding projected conditional rates <math id="S2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\pi}(x,y\mid C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}^{\pi}(x,y\mid C)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Even though the target path is defined through the auxiliary process, we can still learn the generator <math id="S2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="S2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> alone by minimizing the Bregman divergence:</p>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Positional Independence Assumption.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For product spaces <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}^{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝕏</mi><mi>L</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}^{L}</annotation></semantics></math> like the space of sequences, the size of the general rate matrix grows exponentially with the length <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>. To avoid this, sparsity is introduced into the rate matrix by assuming per-position independence of the target conditional probability <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t|C}(x_{t}|c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t|C}(x_{t}|c)</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t|C}(x_{t}|c)=\prod_{i=1}^{L}p_{t|C}^{i}(x_{t}^{i}|c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t|C}(x_{t}|c)=\prod_{i=1}^{L}p_{t|C}^{i}(x_{t}^{i}|c)</annotation></semantics></math>, where the superscript <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th position, which results in the corresponding rate matrix being a mixture of per-position rates <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Campbell et al., 2022</a>)</cite>:</p>
<table id="S2.EGx6" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S2.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sub(x,i,y^{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>sub</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sub(x,i,y^{i})</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the sequence obtained my replacing the token at <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-position in <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{\lnot i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">¬</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{\lnot i}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the sequence <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, with the <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th position excluded.
We will use <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{i}_{t}(x,y^{i}|C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{i}_{t}(x,y^{i}|C)</annotation></semantics></math> to denote <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(x,\,\sub(x,i,y^{i})\mid C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>sub</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(x,\,\sub(x,i,y^{i})\mid C)</annotation></semantics></math> compactly.</p>

<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Variable Length Sequence Generation</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}\coloneqq\bigcup_{k=1}^{L}{\mathbb{V}}^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝕏</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">≔</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>⋃</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msup><mi>𝕍</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}\coloneqq\bigcup_{k=1}^{L}{\mathbb{V}}^{k}</annotation></semantics></math> the space of variable length sequences.
Since there are multiple possible alignments of a partial sequence <math id="S3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> to a clean sequence <math id="S3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, it is not easy to construct conditional marginals <math id="S3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t|C}(x_{t}|x_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t|C}(x_{t}|x_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> as is typically done in masked DFM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Campbell et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gat et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
However, one can use an auxiliary space that include the alignment information and perform projected rate matching.
Similarly to <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al. (2025a)</a></cite>, we define the auxiliary space of partial sequences as <math id="S3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}\coloneqq\bigcup_{k\in[\![L]\!]}{\mathbb{V}}^{k}\times{\mathbb{S}}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">≔</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>⋃</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>L</mi><mpadded style="width:0.158em;" width="0.158em"><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mpadded></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><msup><mi>𝕍</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>𝕊</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}\coloneqq\bigcup_{k\in[\![L]\!]}{\mathbb{V}}^{k}\times{\mathbb{S}}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{S}}_{k}\coloneqq\{(s^{1},\dots,s^{k})\in[\![L]\!]^{k}~|~s^{1}&lt;\dots&lt;s^{k}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝕊</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>L</mi><mpadded style="width:0.108em;" width="0.108em"><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mpadded></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.330em">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">⋯</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{S}}_{k}\coloneqq\{(s^{1},\dots,s^{k})\in[\![L]\!]^{k}~|~s^{1}&lt;\dots&lt;s^{k}\}</annotation></semantics></math> is the space of ordered tuples of positions and <math id="S3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is the maximum length. An example element of <math id="S3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math> is shown on the right of <a href="#S0.F1" title="In Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> as the input <math id="S3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{t},s_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{t},s_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> to the generator.
Additionally, we note a useful isomorphism.
Let <span id="S3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;">[D]</span> be a special token outside the vocabulary <math id="S3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕍</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{V}}</annotation></semantics></math> that is used to indicate a dropped position. Then <math id="S3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathbb{Z}}\coloneqq({\mathbb{V}}\cup\{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}\})^{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>≔</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝕍</mi><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#264690">[D]</mtext><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>L</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathbb{Z}}\coloneqq({\mathbb{V}}\cup\{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}\})^{L}</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to <math id="S3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math> through the mapping <math id="S3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{contract}}:\bar{\mathbb{Z}}\to{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>contract</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{contract}}:\bar{\mathbb{Z}}\to{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math> that removes the <span id="S3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;">[D]</span> tokens from the <math id="S3.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{z}</annotation></semantics></math> to form <math id="S3.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, and moves the exact position information to <math id="S3.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝒔</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{s}</annotation></semantics></math> to produce <math id="S3.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=(x,\bm{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝒔</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=(x,\bm{s})</annotation></semantics></math>.
For example, as shown in <a href="#S0.F1" title="In Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, for <math id="S3.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=8</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{z}=({\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}},{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}},c,{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}},{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}},f,{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}},{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#990000">[M]</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#264690">[D]</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#990000">[M]</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext mathcolor="#990000">[M]</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#990000">[M]</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{z}=({\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}},{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}},c,{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}},{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}},f,{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}},{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{contract}}(\bar{z})=(({\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}},c,{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}},f,{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}},{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}}),(1,3,4,6,7,8))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>contract</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover From this point on, we will use <math id="S3.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> to mean an element of <math id="S3.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S3.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math> interchangeably. 
Finally, we denote <math id="S3.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{rm-drop}}:\bar{\mathbb{Z}}\to{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>rm-drop</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>𝕏</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{rm-drop}}:\bar{\mathbb{Z}}\to{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> to be the function that removes the exact position to produce a sequence in the original space, i.e., for our previous example, <math id="S3.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{rm-drop}}(\bar{z})=(a,b,c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>rm-drop</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{rm-drop}}(\bar{z})=(a,b,c)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Mixture paths in the auxiliary space.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We construct mixture paths on <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math> by setting the conditioning variable as <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(z_{1},z_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(z_{1},z_{0})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{1}=\left(x_{1}\odot{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}\overset{L-\text{len}(x_{1})}{\dots}{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}~,~~[\![L]\!]\right)" and <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0}={\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}\overset{L}{\dots}{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#264690">[D]</mtext><mo with <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\odot" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊙</mo><annotation The goal is to define per-position target rates such that the transition <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}}\to z_{1}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#264690">[D]</mtext><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#990000">[M]</mtext><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}}\to z_{1}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> occurs for each position <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{1}^{i}\neq{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>≠</mo><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#264690">[D]</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{1}^{i}\neq{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}</annotation></semantics></math> such that we can express a tractable distribution over the orderings of insertion and unmasking events for the entire sequence, which can be learned along with the generator parameters.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Learnable Order Dynamics</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Any regular CTMC over countable state space can be represented using a Poisson process and an embedded state transition kernel.
Therefore, we define the per-position target rates as</p>

<tbody id="S3.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle R^{i}_{t}(z,w^{i}\mid(z_{1},z_{0}))=\lambda_{t}^{i}(z;(z_{1},z_{0}))\cdot K^{i}_{t}(z,w^{i}\mid(z_{1},z_{0}))," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle R^{i}_{t}(z,w^{i}\mid(z_{1},z_{0}))=\lambda_{t}^{i}(z;(z_{1},z_{0}))\cdot K^{i}_{t}(z,w^{i}\mid(z_{1},z_{0})),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{t}^{i}(z;(z_{1},z_{0}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{t}^{i}(z;(z_{1},z_{0}))</annotation></semantics></math> is the state and time dependent arrival rate of the Poisson process, and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K^{i}_{t}(z,w^{i}\mid(z_{1},z_{0}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K^{i}_{t}(z,w^{i}\mid(z_{1},z_{0}))</annotation></semantics></math> is the state transition kernel, i.e, when an arrival occurs at the <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th position, the state changes according to the categorical distribution <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K^{i}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K^{i}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.
In order for <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(z,w)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(z,w)</annotation></semantics></math> to be a valid rate, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{t}^{i}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{t}^{i}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K^{i}_{t}(z,z^{i})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K^{i}_{t}(z,z^{i})=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
This characterization allows us to express the order dynamics by controlling the hazard rates, without changing the terminal state distributions of the process.
For our case of two events per position, <span id="S3.SS1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;"> insertion</span> and <span id="S3.SS1.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;"> unmasking</span>, we denote the respective event times as <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}^{i}\coloneqq T^{i}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></mmultiscripts><mo>≔</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}^{i}\coloneqq T^{i}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}\coloneqq T^{i}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></mmultiscripts><mo>≔</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}\coloneqq T^{i}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The left side of <a href="#S0.F1" title="In Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> provides an intuitive illustration of the induced order dynamics.

<a href="#Thmproposition1" title="Proposition 1 (Target conditional rates). ‣ 3.1 Learnable Order Dynamics ‣ 3 Variable Length Sequence Generation ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> shows that the target rates that generate the desired conditional probability flow can be expressed using two increasing right continuous functions.
Note that since <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0}={\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}\overset{L}{\dots}{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#264690">[D]</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝐿</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#264690">[D]</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0}={\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}\overset{L}{\dots}{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is fixed, we will hide the dependence on <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> from the notation for brevity.</p>
</div>

<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.1.1 </span>Parameterization</h4>

<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_floatright" style="width:35%;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18695v1/kumaraswamy_cdf_effect_of_ab_compact.svg" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:167/182;" width="167" height="182"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S3.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Kumaraswamy CDF shapes for different parameter values.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">By learning the parameters <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> governing <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{*}^{\phi,i}:[0,1]\times{\mathbb{Z}}\to[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mo>∗</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{*}^{\phi,i}:[0,1]\times{\mathbb{Z}}\to[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> of <a href="#Thmproposition1" title="Proposition 1 (Target conditional rates). ‣ 3.1 Learnable Order Dynamics ‣ 3 Variable Length Sequence Generation ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> we can learn the target order dynamics.
The choice of the functional form of <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{*}</annotation></semantics></math> depends on the analytical tractability of the resulting <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{\phi}_{t}(z|z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{\phi}_{t}(z|z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Specifically, we need to be able to sample <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}\sim p^{\phi}_{t}(z|z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}\sim p^{\phi}_{t}(z|z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> (ideally using inverse CDF sampling) in order to compute the projected rate matching loss (<a href="#S2.E5" title="In 2 Preliminaries: Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) and also be able to compute the likelihood <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{\phi}_{t}(z|z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{\phi}_{t}(z|z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> for updating <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>, ideally in closed form to avoid numerical integration.
Note that since the likelihood is independent per-position, if we satisfy the desiderata stated above, we obtain an efficient training procedure as discussed in <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Training ‣ 3 Variable Length Sequence Generation ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>.
As discussed in Appendix <a href="#A4.SS2" title="D.2 Likelihood under ϕ ‣ Appendix D Variable length masked diffusion with learnable order dynamics ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.2</span></a>, the likelihood <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{\phi}_{t}(z|z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{\phi}_{t}(z|z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> requires computing the following integral:</p>

<p id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">is an ideal candidate for the functional form of <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{*}</annotation></semantics></math> as it allows inverse CDF sampling, can produce internal modes, and for <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}=a^{i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}=a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}=a^{i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}=a</annotation></semantics></math>, allows us to obtain closed form expressions for the likelihood (see Appendix <a href="#A4.SS5.SSS3" title="D.5.3 Kumaraswamy schedules ‣ D.5 Gradient computation ‣ Appendix D Variable length masked diffusion with learnable order dynamics ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.5.3</span></a> for more details).
Therefore, we parameterize <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b^{\phi,i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}(z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b^{\phi,i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}(z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b^{\phi,i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}(z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b^{\phi,i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}(z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> by a transformer with weights represented by <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>, and set <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}=a^{i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}=a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}=a^{i}_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}=a</annotation></semantics></math> to be a constant, which yields the following closed form expressions for the hazard rates:</p>

</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Interestingly, in this final form, we can see that the shape function <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{at^{a-1}}{1-t^{a}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{at^{a-1}}{1-t^{a}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the same for both insertion and unmasking, and only the hazard rate multipliers <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}</annotation></semantics></math> control the overall rate.
Under the time-change <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=-\log(1-t^{a})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=-\log(1-t^{a})</annotation></semantics></math>, it becomes and exponential race with the parameters <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}</annotation></semantics></math> with precedence constraints (insertion before unmasking).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">where the expectation is over <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{1}\sim p_{\text{data}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>data</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{1}\sim p_{\text{data}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}\sim p_{t|z_{1}}^{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mi>ϕ</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}\sim p_{t|z_{1}}^{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{t}=f_{\text{rm-drop}}(z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>rm-drop</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{t}=f_{\text{rm-drop}}(z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>. The Bregman divergence <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\psi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>ψ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\psi}</annotation></semantics></math> is computed using the negative entropy function <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi(r)=\sum_{k}r_{k}\log r_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi(r)=\sum_{k}r_{k}\log r_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We provide a step-by-step derivation of the training objective in Appendix <a href="#A4.SS4" title="D.4 Loss function ‣ Appendix D Variable length masked diffusion with learnable order dynamics ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.4</span></a>.
Furthermore, <a href="#Thmproposition5" title="Proposition 5 (Projected rate matching upper bounds terminal KL). ‣ C.0.1 Projected rate matching ‣ Appendix C Projected Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS0.SSS1" title="C.0.1 Projected rate matching ‣ Appendix C Projected Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.0.1</span></a> shows that using the standard argument of using KL-divergence between CTMC path measures, followed by the data processing inequality, this loss maximizes a lower bound on the data log-likelihood under the generator.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmremark1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmremark1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Remark 1</span></span><span id="Thmremark1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmremark1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmremark1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the case of fixed <math id="Thmremark1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="Thmremark1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{i,\phi}_{*}=b^{i,\phi}_{*}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mo>∗</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mo>∗</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{i,\phi}_{*}=b^{i,\phi}_{*}=1</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="Thmremark1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, the Bregman divergence <math id="Thmremark1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D(\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{\phi},\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{\theta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>ϕ</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{\phi},\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{\theta})</annotation></semantics></math> becomes zero, and we obtain the loss equivalent to FlexMDM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> written in terms of rates instead of posterior probabilities.
Therefore, we call our method LFlexMDM, where L stands for learnable order dynamics.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmremark2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmremark2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Remark 2</span></span><span id="Thmremark2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> </span>(Schedule regularization)<span id="Thmremark2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmremark2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmremark2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since both the generator and target rates are trainable, they can take extreme values creating numerical degeneracy in the training. To discourage such degenerate schedules, we add a schedule regularization term as described in Appendix <a href="#A4.SS5.SSS2" title="D.5.2 Schedule regularization ‣ D.5 Gradient computation ‣ Appendix D Variable length masked diffusion with learnable order dynamics ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.5.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.2.1 </span>Gradient computation</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since the expectation depends on the target rate network parameters <math id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>, we resort to score based gradient estimation for <math id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> and use REINFORCE leave-one-out <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kool et al., 2019</a>)</cite> to reduce variance with minimal impact on training efficiency.
