<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Sampling</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in <a href="#S0.F1" title="In Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> on the bottom right, generator network predicts the rates <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}},t}^{\theta,i}(x_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}},t}^{\theta,i}(x_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> for insertion at gap position <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}},t}^{\theta,i}(x_{t})~K^{\theta,i}(\cdot|x_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.330em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>K</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}},t}^{\theta,i}(x_{t})~K^{\theta,i}(\cdot|x_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> for unmasking at masked position <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>.
We use a simple <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-leaping sampler <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gillespie, 2001</a>)</cite> that allows to sample multiple events simultaneously. Additionally, the guarantee for the correctness of adaptive sampling from FlexMDM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> extends to LFlexMDM. The complete sampling algorithm is shown in <a href="#alg2" title="In 3.3 Sampling ‣ 3 Variable Length Sequence Generation ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>

<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Related Work</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For discrete diffusion, there exist different <em id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">fixed</em> noising processes like uniform noising, masking, or a mixture of both <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sahoo et al., 2024b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Schiff et al., </a>; <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
For masked diffusion, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al. (2025b)</a></cite> show that the order of denoising is crucial for the generative abilities of diffusion models, and the typical noising process that uses a uniform masking schedule may not be able to exploit the structure present in discrete sequences, thereby limiting the generators ability.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al. (2025)</a></cite> looks at learning of generation order in any-order models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hoogeboom et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Uria et al., 2013</a>)</cite>, which have been shown to be equivalent to fixed length unmasking models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ou et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. However, they work with the fixed length formulation using a Placket-Luce model for the generation order.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The useful desiderata of <span id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">i)</span> modeling distributions over variable-length sequences and <span id="S4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">ii)</span> the ability to insert tokens have inspired a number of recent works to move away from fixed-window text diffusion towards insertion- and substitution- based discrete flow models in which positions during the generation process acquire a relative rather than absolute interpretation.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Patel et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> proposes Insertion Language Model (ILM) that generates sequences by jointly modeling the distribution over the insertion location and the vocabulary.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Havasi et al. (2025)</a></cite> proposed EditFlows that uses the projected DFM to construct a generator CTMC that models the rates of insertion, deletion, and substitution operations. However, both these models can only insert one token per gap at a time.
FlexMDM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> can insert multiple mask tokens per gap.
But the flexibility comes at a cost.
The action space of insertion based generation is larger than that of unmasking based models, and there have been limited attempts to explore learning the generation order in insertion based models. Most of the exiting works focus on models that insert one token at a time and require simulating the generation trajectory for learning the generation order <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gu et al., 2019</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Brantley et al., 2019</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">

<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Experiments</h2>

<figure id="S5.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18695v1/fix_b_um_loss_comparison.svg" id="S5.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/233;" width="381" height="233"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S5.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Loss comparison for the hard star graph traversal task with and without fixing target unmasking rate (<math id="S5.F6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>). The erratic dynamics of a fully unconstrained set of target rates motivates freezing <math id="S5.F6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Model.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For all our experiments, we use DDiT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lou et al., 2023</a>)</cite> with RoPE, and adaptive layer-norm (AdaLN) for conditioning on the time variable <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Peebles &amp; Xie, 2023</a>)</cite>.
We implement the target and generator rates
with MLP scalar heads on top of the transformer.
For FlexMDM (baseline), we follow the setup in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al. (2025a)</a></cite>, which also uses DDiT architecture, but has a length prediction head for insertion instead of a rate prediction head.
We experiment with a “separate” setting where the target rates are predicted by a separate auxiliary transformer, and with a memory-efficient “shared” setting where all heads share the same backbone transformer, which is updated by both the <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> components of the <a href="#S3.Ex7" title="In 3.2.1 Gradient computation ‣ 3.2 Training ‣ 3 Variable Length Sequence Generation ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> gradient estimator.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Graph Traversal</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dataset.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the star graphs dataset from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Patel et al. (2025b)</a></cite>. <span id="footnote3" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">3</span>
                
                
                
                
                
                
                
              See <a href="#A5.SS1" title="E.1 Graph Traversal ‣ Appendix E Details of the experiment setup ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.1</span></a> for more details.</span></span></span>
It consists of star shaped graphs with one junction node and multiple arms coming in and out of the junction node.
The task is to produce a path from the given starting and terminal nodes.
The input graph is stringified as edge pairs arranged in a random order (the order is random but remains fixed for a given graph). The input string is this stringified graph followed by the starting and terminal nodes, the model needs to generate the path (edges in the correct order) connecting the starting and terminal nodes.
We use the medium and hard difficulty settings of the dataset as both of these use graphs with variable arm lengths. The graphs in the hard setting vary significantly in the number of arms as well as the arm lengths, making it a challenging task.
However, if the edges of output path are generated starting from the end points moving towards the junction node, then the task becomes trivial even for a local model, i.e., a model that does not plan ahead.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.1.1 </span>Design choices</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the graph traversal to explore the design choices for parameterizing the target hazard rates <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{t}^{\phi,i}(z;\,z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{t}^{\phi,i}(z;\,z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Flexibility <span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">vs</span> Stability</span>:  As noted in <a href="#S3.SS1.SSS1" title="3.1.1 Parameterization ‣ 3.1 Learnable Order Dynamics ‣ 3 Variable Length Sequence Generation ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1.1</span></a>, the hazard rates have have two free parameters for each position, <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mmultiscripts><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></mmultiscripts><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mmultiscripts><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></mmultiscripts><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We first examine the effect of flexibility of the target rate model <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{t}^{\phi,i}(z;\,z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{t}^{\phi,i}(z;\,z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Interestingly, the performance of the generator improves when the <span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unmasking</span> target rate <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}</annotation></semantics></math> is fixed (
<span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_inline-block fas fa-snowflake" aria-hidden="true">
</span>) as opposed to trainable (
<span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_inline-block fas fa-fire" aria-hidden="true">
</span>), as seen from the slight improvement in medium difficulty and a significant improvement in hard difficulty LFlexMDM (<a href="#S4.T1" title="In Figure 4 ‣ 4 Related Work ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, line <span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;"> 5</span> <span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">vs</span> line <span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;"> 6</span>).
<a href="#A6.F9" title="In F.1 Flexibility vs Stability ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analyses ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>,
which presents the loss comparison for the hard star graph traversal task with and without fixing target unmasking rate (<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>), shows that the additional flexibility in learning <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}</annotation></semantics></math> destabilizes the training.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Note that fixing <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}</annotation></semantics></math> still leaves enough room for learning of insertion order, i.e., if <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}&lt;h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}&lt;h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, then for any <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{P}}({T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}\leq t\mid{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}=h_{1})&lt;{\mathbb{P}}({T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}\leq t\mid{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}=h_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{P}}({T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}\leq t\mid{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}=h_{1})&lt;{\mathbb{P}}({T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}\leq t\mid{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}=h_{2})</annotation></semantics></math>. The preference for unmasking orders will show up in <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K^{\theta,i}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K^{\theta,i}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> values, which can be used for confidence-based position selection during decoding.
Based on this observation, we fix <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math> in the subsequent experiments.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Shared <span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">vs</span> Separate Backbone</span>:  Additionally, we explore the use of a shared DDiT backbone for the target rate model and generator.
For the hard version of the star graph traversal task, using a shared backbone leads to considerable drop in performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.1.2 </span>Analysis: Generation Order</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We also investigate whether the introduction of learnable target rates allows the generator to learn to generate the sequences in the optimal order.
The optimal <em id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">local</em> order for star graphs starts from the end points of the arm and moves towards the junction.
We analyze examples of the complete history of the generation under LFlexMDM and FlexMDM. As shown in the example in <a href="#S4.F4" title="In 4 Related Work ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, LFlexMDM indeed learns to generate in the optimal order.
To inspect this further, we compute the correlation between the generation order and distance from the junction node. Since the arm lengths vary significantly for the hard version of the task, we normalize both the generation order and distance from the junction node by the path length.
<a href="#S4.F5" title="In 4 Related Work ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows the correlation between the generation order (normalized by path length) and normalized distance from the junction node.
The ideal correlation for optimal local order should be -1. Interestingly, we observe that LFlexMDM with trainable <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}</annotation></semantics></math> (line <span id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;"> 5</span> in <a href="#S4.T1" title="In Figure 4 ‣ 4 Related Work ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) achieves mean correlation of <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.91" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.91</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.91</annotation></semantics></math>, when compared to <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.22" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.22</annotation></semantics></math> for the case when we fix <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math> (line <span id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;"> 6</span>) and do not use confidence-based position selection during inference (line <span id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;"> 7</span> in <a href="#S4.T1" title="In Figure 4 ‣ 4 Related Work ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). Using confidence-based position selection for the fixed <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math> case achieves a mean correlation of <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.60</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.60</annotation></semantics></math>. This supports our initial observation in <a href="#S5.SS1.SSS1" title="5.1.1 Design choices ‣ 5.1 Graph Traversal ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1.1</span></a> that fixing <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math> stabilizes the training while still providing enough room for learning of ideal insertion order, which can be elicited even in the unmasking steps by confidence-based position selection.
Interestingly, using confidence-based position selection for FlexMDM changes the correlation from <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.09" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.09</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.09</annotation></semantics></math> (light red) to <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.33" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.33</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.33</annotation></semantics></math> (dark red), lower than the respective correlation for LFlexMDM with fixed <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math> (light blue to dark blue).</p>
</div>

<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Small Molecule Generation</h3>

<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dataset.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train all the models on the SAFE dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Noutahi et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, which consists of molecules from ZINC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Irwin et al., 2012</a>)</cite> and UniChem <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chambers et al., 2013</a>)</cite>.
Following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al. (2025)</a></cite>, we train for 50k steps with a global batch size of 2048.
Based on the results of the graph traversal experiments, we fix the unmasking rate <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}^{\phi}=b_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}^{\theta}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>ϕ</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}^{\phi}=b_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}^{\theta}=1</annotation></semantics></math> and only keep the target insertion rate <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}^{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mi>ϕ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}^{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> trainable.
We evaluate on <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">de novo</span> generation by sampling 1000 molecules unconditionally from the trained models and compute the metrics of <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">validity</span>, <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">uniqueness</span>, <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">diversity</span>, and <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">quality</span>. <a href="#S5.T2" title="In 5.1.2 Analysis: Generation Order ‣ 5.1 Graph Traversal ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows the results, and we provide a detailed analysis below.</p>
<ul id="S5.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:0pt;">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Fixed window vs. variable length</span>: For MDM, following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al. (2025)</a></cite> we sample the lengths of the mask chunks from the ZINC250k distribution even for <span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">de novo</span> generation. However, for FlexMDM and LFlexMDM, we perform completely unconstrained generation starting from a blank canvas. This highlights the advantage of working with a variable-length model.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Diversity-quality trade-off</span>: As seen in <a href="#S5.T2" title="In 5.1.2 Analysis: Generation Order ‣ 5.1 Graph Traversal ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, LFlexMDM shows improvement in validity and quality over FlexMDM, with a slight decrease in diversity. Indeed, this duality is expected because learning structurally good generation orders intuitively corresponds to reducing the randomness. <a href="#S5.F7" title="In 5.1.2 Analysis: Generation Order ‣ 5.1 Graph Traversal ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> (right) shows the plot of quality/validity vs. diversity as we vary the nucleus sampling <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> cut-off (<a href="#alg2" title="In 3.3 Sampling ‣ 3 Variable Length Sequence Generation ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> line 25). We observe that LFlexMDM improves significantly in quality (<math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mphantom></mphantom><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{}</annotation></semantics></math> 50% vs 60%) we reduce the randomness (lower <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> values) in the sampling process.
In the same vein, uniqueness drops slightly, but validity improves, when we employ confidence-based position selection during decoding (lines 20-23), as opposed to sampling uniformly from eligible positions (line 18), making decoding more greedy.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"> 
<div id="S5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Effect of inference budget</span>: Next we fix the sampling parameters to their respective best values and vary the sampling steps. As seen in <a href="#S5.F7" title="In 5.1.2 Analysis: Generation Order ‣ 5.1 Graph Traversal ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> (left), <span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LFlexMDM shows consistent and significant improvement over FlexMDM in quality and validity at all sampling budgets</span>.
<span id="footnote4" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup>
                      <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">4</span>
                      
                      
                      
                      
                      
                      
                      
                    Results with additional nucleus-sampling <math id="footnote4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> values, as well as a shared-backbone implemenetation, are provided in <a href="#A6.T7" title='In Fixing target unmasking rate (𝑏_"um"=1) ‣ F.2.1 Examples: Generation Order ‣ F.2 Star Graph Traversal ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analyses ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics' class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.</span></span></span></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>

<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce learnable order dynamics into variable-length unmasking DFM, allowing the model to learn to generate in favorable orders.
By incorporating data-dependent insertion and unmasking rates, the model successfully learns task-specific optimal orders, when such an order exists, e.g. for graph traversal.
The experiments on <span id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">de novo</span> molecule generation demonstrate that learned order dynamics lead to significant improvements in the validity and quality of generated samples compared to the baseline that does not use learned order dynamics.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Future Work:</span> While the simultaneous simultaneous training of the generator and target rates using a single backward pass per example is relatively efficient, there is room for further improvement.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents work whose goal is to advance the field of Machine
Learning. There are many potential societal consequences of our work, none
which we feel must be specifically highlighted here.</p>
</div>

<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Background: Discrete Flow Matching</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Markov Processes on Discrete Spaces</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> be countable set (e.g. the vocabulary <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕍</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{V}}</annotation></semantics></math> or the space of sequences of length <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> with tokens from <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕍</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{V}}</annotation></semantics></math>), and <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> be a continuous time stochastic process on <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<p id="A2.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math> is the <em id="A2.SS1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">rate</em> of the transition from <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> at time <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, such that <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="R_{t}(x,x)=-\sum_{y\neq x}R_{t}(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.055em">−</mo><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(x,x)=-\sum_{y\neq x}R_{t}(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math>. Equivalently, <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(x,y)=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{{\mathbb{P}}(X_{t+h}=y|X_{t}=x)-\delta_{x}(y)}{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(x,y)=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{{\mathbb{P}}(X_{t+h}=y|X_{t}=x)-\delta_{x}(y)}{h}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>

<div id="Thmdefinition1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefinition1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 1</span></span><span id="Thmdefinition1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Time marginals generated by CTMC)<span id="Thmdefinition1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefinition1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefinition1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We note that the following statements are equivalent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Campbell et al., 2024</a>)</cite>:</p>
<ul id="A2.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(\cdot,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(\cdot,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">generates</span> <math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(\cdot,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(\cdot,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy the KFE in the marginal form (<a href="#A2.E14" title="In B.1 Markov Processes on Discrete Spaces ‣ Appendix B Background: Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A Markov process <math id="A2.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> with rates <math id="A2.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(\cdot,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(\cdot,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> and initial distribution <math id="A2.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> has <math id="A2.I1.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> as its marginal distribution at time <math id="A2.I1.i3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.1.1 </span>Indexed Collections of CTMCs</h4>

<div id="Thmdefinition2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefinition2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 2</span></span><span id="Thmdefinition2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Conditional Rates)<span id="Thmdefinition2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefinition2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefinition2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a general variable <math id="Thmdefinition2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C\in\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C\in\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math> with distribution <math id="Thmdefinition2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<ul id="A2.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">denote <math id="A2.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> dependent rates as <math id="A2.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(x,y|C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(x,y|C)</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">denote by <math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left\{\{X_{t}^{c}\}\right\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\{\{X_{t}^{c}\}\right\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}}</annotation></semantics></math> a collection of CTMCs on <math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> with rates <math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(x,y|C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(x,y|C)</annotation></semantics></math> and initial distribution <math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{0}(x|C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{0}(x|C)</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A2.I2.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t|C}(x|c)\coloneqq{\mathbb{P}}(X_{t}^{c}=x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t|C}(x|c)\coloneqq{\mathbb{P}}(X_{t}^{c}=x)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the marginals of the CTMC <math id="A2.I2.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X_{t}^{c}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X_{t}^{c}\}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the special case of endpoint indexed collection, we have <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=(X_{0},X_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=(X_{0},X_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{1}\sim p_{\text{data}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>data</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{1}\sim p_{\text{data}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{0}\sim\pi(x_{0}|x_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{0}\sim\pi(x_{0}|x_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is the coupling distribution <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gat et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmproposition2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmproposition2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 2</span></span><span id="Thmproposition2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Mixture of CTMCs)<span id="Thmproposition2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmproposition2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproposition2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The mixture rate <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="R_{t}(x,\cdot)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{C|X_{t}=x}[R_{t}(x,\cdot|C)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(x,\cdot)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{C|X_{t}=x}[R_{t}(x,\cdot|C)]</annotation></semantics></math> <em id="Thmproposition2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">generates</em> the marginals <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}(x)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{C}[p_{t|C}(x|C)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mi>C</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}(x)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{C}[p_{t|C}(x|C)]</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The proof assumes mild regularity conditions and follows from a straightforward application of the KFE (see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Campbell et al. (2024)</a></cite> or <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lipman et al. (2024b)</a></cite> Thm. 14 for details).
This result shows there exists a rate matrix <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="R_{t}(\cdot,\cdot)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{C}[R_{t}(\cdot,\cdot|C)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mi>C</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(\cdot,\cdot)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{C}[R_{t}(\cdot,\cdot|C)]</annotation></semantics></math> and the corresponding CTMC <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> <em id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">generates</em> <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}(x)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{C}[p_{t|C}(x|C)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mi>C</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}(x)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{C}[p_{t|C}(x|C)]</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore, in order to sample from the data distribution <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, we can follow:</p>
<ol id="A2.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A2.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Pick the indexing set <math id="A2.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=(X_{0},X_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=(X_{0},X_{1})</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Use <math id="A2.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}=p_{\text{data}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>data</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}=p_{\text{data}}</annotation></semantics></math> and pick the coupling distribution <math id="A2.I3.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(x_{0}|x_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(x_{0}|x_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>, typically independent i.e. <math id="A2.I3.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(x_{0}|x_{1})=p_{0}(x_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(x_{0}|x_{1})=p_{0}(x_{0})</annotation></semantics></math> for some easy to sample <math id="A2.I3.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Construct a collection of CTMCs <math id="A2.I3.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X_{t}^{c}\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X_{t}^{c}\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}}</annotation></semantics></math> with rates <math id="A2.I3.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(x,y|C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(x,y|C)</annotation></semantics></math> such that it <em id="A2.I3.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">generates</em> <math id="A2.I3.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t|C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t|C}</annotation></semantics></math>, which satisfies <math id="A2.I3.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1|C}(x|x_{1},x_{0})=\delta_{x_{1}}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo <section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We want to learn the rates <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math> using a parametric model <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{\theta}_{t}(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{\theta}_{t}(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math>. Since we can easily write down the conditional rates <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}(x,y|z)" display="inline" match <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{\theta}_{t}(x,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{\theta}_{t}(x,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="R_{t}(x,\cdot)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim That is for some distance measure <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>, we want to minimize:</p>

<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">

<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Convexity in the first argument</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">It is convex in the first argument. Meaning that <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda D_{F}(b_{1},a)+(1-\lambda)D_{F}(b_{2},a)\geq D_{F}(\lambda b_{1}+(1-\lambda)b_{2},a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda D_{F}(b_{1},a)+(1-\lambda)D_{F}(b_{2},a)\geq D_{F}(\lambda b_{1}+(1-\lambda)b_{2},a)</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.
This is easy to see:</p>
<table id="A2.EGx19" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Gradient is linear for convex combinations in the first argument.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Its gradient with respect to the second argument is <span id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">linear</span> w.r.t affine combinations in the first argument <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Holderrieth et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
This is a consequence of the expression for the gradient w.r.t the second argument, which is given by</p>
<table id="A2.EGx20" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.E17"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\nabla_{a}D_{F}(b,a)=-\nabla^{2}F(a)(b-a)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>a</mi></msub><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>F</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\nabla_{a}D_{F}(b,a)=-\nabla^{2}F(a)(b-a),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla^{2}F(a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mo>∇</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>F</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla^{2}F(a)</annotation></semantics></math> is the Hessian of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>.
Clearly, <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(b)=\nabla_{a}D_{F}(b,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>a</mi></msub><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(b)=\nabla_{a}D_{F}(b,a)</annotation></semantics></math> is linear in <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>.
Therefore, under convex combinations, which can be extended to expectations, we get:</p>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Therefore for <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=X_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=X_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> we can use the following objective to train the parameters of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{\theta}_{t}(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{\theta}_{t}(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Projected Discrete Flow Matching</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we will discuss a type of <em id="A3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">weak</em> intertwining of two Markov processes that depends on the law of the main process. This is a generalization of the flow matching with auxiliary variables <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Havasi et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and the joint interpolants <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, in that we allow probabilistic mappings between the two spaces.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math> be two countable state spaces, and let <math id="A3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{enc}}(x|z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>enc</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{enc}}(x|z)</annotation></semantics></math> be probability kernel from <math id="A3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefinition3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3</span></span><span id="Thmdefinition3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefinition3.p1" class="ltx_para">

Then the CTMC <math id="Thmdefinition3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="Thmdefinition3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> with rate matrix <math id="Thmdefinition3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> is said to be a <em id="Thmdefinition3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">weakly intertwined projection</em> of <math id="Thmdefinition3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> under the encoder <math id="Thmdefinition3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{enc}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>enc</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{enc}}</annotation></semantics></math> if</p>
