<div id="Thmproposition3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmproposition3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 3</span></span><span id="Thmproposition3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<math id="Thmproposition3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{\pi}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{\pi}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> generates <math id="Thmproposition3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>)<span id="Thmproposition3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmproposition3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproposition3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmproposition3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> be a weakly intertwined projection of <math id="Thmproposition3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{Z_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{Z_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> under the encoder <math id="Thmproposition3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{enc}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">enc</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{enc}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="Thmproposition3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> as defined in <a href="#A3.E20" title="In Definition 3. ‣ Appendix C Projected Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> generates <math id="Thmproposition3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> in the sense of <a href="#Thmdefinition1" title="Definition 1 (Time marginals generated by CTMC). ‣ B.1 Markov Processes on Discrete Spaces ‣ Appendix B Background: Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Definition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</span></p>

<div id="A3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">We can easily see that <math id="A3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> <em id="A3.p3.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">generates</em> <math id="A3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}(x)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim p_{t}}[\pi_{\text{enc}}(x|z)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>enc</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}(x)=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim p_{t}}[\pi_{\text{enc}}(x|z)]</annotation></semantics></math> by checking the KFE:</span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx25" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex15"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<div id="Thmremark3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmremark3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Remark 3</span></span><span id="Thmremark3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> </span>(Degenerate (Dirac) decoders preserve the KFE)<span id="Thmremark3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmremark3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmremark3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Bayes decoder <math id="Thmremark3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{dec,t}}(z|x,C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>dec,t</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{dec,t}}(z|x,C)</annotation></semantics></math> in <a href="#A3.E23" title="In Appendix C Projected Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a> averages over all latent states <math id="Thmremark3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> compatible with the observed state <math id="Thmremark3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> (and condition <math id="Thmremark3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>). As we will see later that we can additionally condition on <em id="Thmremark3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">side information</em> <math id="Thmremark3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., an alignment/position tuple) such that the latent state can be selected deterministically from <math id="Thmremark3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,H)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,H)</annotation></semantics></math>. In this case we can use a degenerate decoder</p>

<div id="A3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Following is the key result stating that the projected rates generate the desired time marginals just like vanilla DFM without auxiliary variables.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmproposition4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmproposition4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 4</span></span><span id="Thmproposition4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<math id="Thmproposition4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{\pi}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{\pi}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> generates <math id="Thmproposition4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>)<span id="Thmproposition4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmproposition4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproposition4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmproposition4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> be a weakly intertwined projection of <math id="Thmproposition4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{Z_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{Z_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> under the encoder <math id="Thmproposition4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{enc}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">enc</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{enc}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="Thmproposition4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> as defined in <a href="#A3.E20" title="In Definition 3. ‣ Appendix C Projected Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> generates <math id="Thmproposition4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> in the sense of <a href="#Thmdefinition1" title="Definition 1 (Time marginals generated by CTMC). ‣ B.1 Markov Processes on Discrete Spaces ‣ Appendix B Background: Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Definition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</span></p>

<math id="A3.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation This approach comes in handy when it is easier to construct probability path on the auxiliary space <math id="A3.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math> than the original space <math id="A3.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<section id="A3.SS0.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.0.1 </span>Projected rate matching</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Even though the probability paths are constructed in the auxiliary space, we still want to learn the rates in the original space <math id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<p id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The question, however, is whether this is the same as</p>

<p id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Due to the convexity in the first argument of Bregman divergence, we see that the two expressions are not equal in general: the first one is an upper bound for the second one.</p>

<div id="Thmproposition5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmproposition5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 5</span></span><span id="Thmproposition5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Projected rate matching upper bounds terminal KL)<span id="Thmproposition5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmproposition5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproposition5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X_{t}\}_{t\in[0,1]}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X_{t}\}_{t\in[0,1]}</annotation></semantics></math> be a time-inhomogeneous CTMC on <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> with initial distribution <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and (marginal) projected rates <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\pi}(\cdot,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}^{\pi}(\cdot,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{X}_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{X}_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> be another CTMC on <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{X}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{X}}</annotation></semantics></math> with the same initial distribution <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and model rates <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\theta}(\cdot,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}^{\theta}(\cdot,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. Assume absolute continuity of the jump intensities: for all <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\neq y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\neq y</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\pi}(x,y)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}^{\pi}(x,y)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> implies <math id="Thmproposition5.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}^{\theta}(x,y)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}^{\theta}(x,y)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, and assume the expectations below are finite.</span></p>
</div>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">The inequality <math id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\text{KL}}(p_{1}^{\pi}\|p_{1}^{\theta})\leq\mathcal{D}_{\text{KL}}(\mathbb{P}^{\pi}\|\mathbb{P}^{\theta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>KL</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>KL</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\text{KL}}(p_{1}^{\pi}\|p_{1}^{\theta})\leq\mathcal{D}_{\text{KL}}(\mathbb{P}^{\pi}\|\mathbb{P}^{\theta})</annotation></semantics></math> follows by data processing inequality, since <math id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> is a measurable function of the full path.
The path-space identity is the standard Radon–Nikodym derivative formula for time-inhomogeneous CTMCs, which yields
<math id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p6.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\text{KL}}(\mathbb{P}^{\pi}\|\mathbb{P}^{\theta})=\int_{0}^{1}\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbb{P}^{\pi}}[D_{F}(R_{t}^{\pi}(X_{t},\cdot),R_{t}^{\theta}(X_{t},\cdot))]\,\mathrm{d}t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>KL</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi>π</mi></msup></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>F</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\text{KL}}(\mathbb{P}^{\pi}\|\mathbb{P}^{\theta})=\int_{0}^{1}\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbb{P}^{\pi}}[D_{F}(R_{t}^{\pi}(X_{t},\cdot),R_{t}^{\theta}(X_{t},\cdot))]\,\mathrm{d}t</annotation></semantics></math>
when <math id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(a)=\sum a\log a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(a)=\sum a\log a</annotation></semantics></math> is applied to the off-diagonal jump intensities.
Finally, the conditional-mixture upper bound is exactly <a href="#A3.E30" title="In C.0.1 Projected rate matching ‣ Appendix C Projected Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">30</span></a> applied pointwise in <math id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, and integrating over <math id="A3.SS0.SSS1.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> gives the final inequality.
For a simple proof using discretization arguments, see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shaul et al. (2025)</a></cite>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Now we have two times <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}</annotation></semantics></math> that need to be sampled ensuring that <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}&lt;{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}&lt;{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., insertion happens before unmasking.</p>

<div id="A4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Notation:</span> In the following, the CDFs <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{\phi,i}(t;z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{\phi,i}(t;z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{\phi,i}(t;z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{\phi,i}(t;z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> depend on the learnable parameters <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> and the target sequence <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>; for brevity we suppress this dependence in the notation and write <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{i}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{i}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> throughout this proof.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">

<p id="A4.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">such that <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{i}(0)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{i}(0)=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{i}(1)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{i}(1)=1</annotation></semantics></math>.
We then define the conditional distribution of <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mmultiscripts><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></mmultiscripts><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> given <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}^{i}=s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></mmultiscripts><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}^{i}=s</annotation></semantics></math> by <span id="A4.SS1.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">truncating</span> a base distribution of a random variable <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[s,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[s,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. Let the base distribution have CDF <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(u)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(u)</annotation></semantics></math>, again
such that <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(0)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(0)=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(1)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(1)=1</annotation></semantics></math>.

<p id="A4.SS1.p4.3" class="ltx_p">for <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. <section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>Training</h3>

<section id="A4.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.3.1 </span>Projected target rates</h4>

<div id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We will now apply the framework of projected rate matching from <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Projected Discrete Flow Matching ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a> to the case of variable length masked diffusion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>.
Before proceeding, recall the key notation.
For variable length masked diffusion, we have an augmented space <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathbb{Z}}_{L}=({\mathbb{V}}\cup\{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}},{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}}\})^{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝕍</mi><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#264690">[D]</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace" mathcolor="#990000">[M]</mtext><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>L</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathbb{Z}}_{L}=({\mathbb{V}}\cup\{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{{\textnormal{{[D]}}}}},{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}{{\textnormal{{[M]}}}}}\})^{L}</annotation></semantics></math> with encoder <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{enc}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>enc</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{enc}}</annotation></semantics></math> that removes <span id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;">[D]</span> tokens. The conditioning variable is <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{z}_{1}=(x_{1},\bm{s}_{1})\in{\mathbb{Z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒛</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒔</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{z}_{1}=(x_{1},\bm{s}_{1})\in{\mathbb{Z}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{1}^{i}=i,~i\in[\len(x_{1})]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.497em">,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>len</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{1}^{i}=i,~i\in[\len(x_{1})]</annotation></semantics></math> are the positions in the ground truth sequence <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>. <span id="footnote5" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">5</span>
                
                
                
                
                
                
                
              Technically, the empty sequence <math id="footnote5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0}=\emptyset" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0}=\emptyset</annotation></semantics></math> is also present in the condition but we will suppress it for brevity.</span></span></span>
Equivalently,
for some intermediate time, <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}\in{\mathbb{S}}_{\len(x_{t})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>𝕊</mi><mrow><mi>len</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}\in{\mathbb{S}}_{\len(x_{t})}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the ordered tuple of non-<span id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;">[D]</span> positions in <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. That is, <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}=(s_{t}^{1},\dots,s_{t}^{\len(x_{t})})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>len</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}=(s_{t}^{1},\dots,s_{t}^{\len(x_{t})})</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}^{1}&lt;\dots&lt;s_{t}^{\len(x_{t})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>&lt;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">⋯</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>len</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}^{1}&lt;\dots&lt;s_{t}^{\len(x_{t})}</annotation></semantics></math> are the positions in <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> that contain non-<span id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;">[D]</span> tokens. Then position <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> in the original space <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to position <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> in the augmented space <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">

<section id="A4.SS5.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.5.1 </span>Full gradient estimator for two parameter sets</h4>

<div id="A4.SS5.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS5.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If we have <math id="A4.SS5.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{\phi,\theta}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{\phi,\theta}(z)</annotation></semantics></math> that depends on two sets of parameters <math id="A4.SS5.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\phi,\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\phi,\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="A4.SS5.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\sim p^{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\sim p^{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>, we need to compute:</p>

Therefore:</p>

rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" \quad+\frac{1}{2}\left[\nabla_{\phi}f^{\phi,\theta}(z_{1})+\nabla_{\phi}f^{\phi,\theta}(z_{2})\right]\\[5.0pt]
\frac{1}{2}\left[\nabla_{\theta}f^{\phi,\theta}(z_{1})+\nabla_{\theta}f^{\phi,\theta}(z_{2})\right]\end{pmatrix}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</section>
<section id="A4.SS5.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.5.2 </span>Schedule regularization</h4>

<div id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> is optimized jointly with <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, <a href="#S3.E11" title="In 3.2 Training ‣ 3 Variable Length Sequence Generation ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> admits degenerate solutions where the insertion/unmasking-time distributions place excessive probability mass near the endpoints <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., delaying most events until <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\approx 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\approx 1</annotation></semantics></math>).
This suppresses the (rate-weighted) prediction term in <a href="#S3.E11" title="In 3.2 Training ‣ 3 Variable Length Sequence Generation ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> and allows the model hazards to match near-zero target hazards with negligible cost.
To discourage such degenerate schedules, we add a sequence level schedule prior, which acts as a regularizer on the target schedule.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We add a loss term to regularize the <em id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">mixture CDF across positions</em> to be close to a straight line <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(t)=t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(t)=t</annotation></semantics></math>. Intuitively, this encourages the marginal event time of a uniformly sampled position to be approximately <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, discouraging excessive mass near <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1</annotation></semantics></math> without prescribing a particular per-position shape.
The mixture CDFs over positions is defined as:</p>

We then add a penalty encouraging <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{F}_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{\phi}(t)\approx t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>F</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext><mi>ϕ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{F}_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{\phi}(t)\approx t</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{F}_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{\phi}(t)\approx t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>F</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>ϕ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{F}_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{\phi}(t)\approx t</annotation></semantics></math>, on a grid <math id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{t_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K}\subset(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{t_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K}\subset(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<div id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS5.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Additionally, we penalize each position separately to stay away from concentrating mass near the endpoints.

<p id="A4.SS5.SSS3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">For <math id="A4.SS5.SSS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\leq t" display="inline" id="A4.SS5.SSS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(t)\leq 1-F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(t)\leq 1-F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}^{i}(s)</annotation></semantics></math>, hence the ratio is in <math id="A4.SS5.SSS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation alttext="[0,F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{i}(t)]\subseteq[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo encoding="application/x-tex">[0,F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}^{i}(t)]\subseteq[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.
In general, the integral does not simplify to elementary functions, but it admits closed forms in certain special cases.</p>

<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Special case <math id="A4.SS5.SSS3.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}=a_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}=a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}=a_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}=a</annotation></semantics></math></h5>

<div id="A4.SS5.SSS3.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS5.SSS3.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A4.SS5.SSS3.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}a_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}}={\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}a_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">a</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">a</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}a_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}}={\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}a_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=a</annotation></semantics></math>, the integral
<math id="A4.SS5.SSS3.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" <section id="A4.SS5.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.5.4 </span>Probability of an order under Kumaraswamy Schedule</h4>

<div id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a sequence of length <math id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{T^{i}\}_{i=1}^{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{T^{i}\}_{i=1}^{L}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the event times, one for each position, such that <math id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{i}\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{i}\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math> almost surely.
Let <math id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi:[L]\to[L]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi:[L]\to[L]</annotation></semantics></math> be a bijection such that <math id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{\pi(1)}&lt;T^{\pi(2)}&lt;\cdots&lt;T^{\pi(L)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo rspace="0.1389em">&lt;</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.1389em">⋯</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em">&lt;</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{\pi(1)}&lt;T^{\pi(2)}&lt;\cdots&lt;T^{\pi(L)}</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is an order over the positions induced by the event times.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Interestingly, we get a nice closed form expression for orders under the Kumaraswamy schedule if we fix <math id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> for all positions (special case 2, mentioned in <a href="#A4.SS5.SSS3" title="D.5.3 Kumaraswamy schedules ‣ D.5 Gradient computation ‣ Appendix D Variable length masked diffusion with learnable order dynamics ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.5.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmproposition6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmproposition6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 6</span></span><span id="Thmproposition6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Probability of an order under Kumaraswamy Schedule)<span id="Thmproposition6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmproposition6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproposition6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="Thmproposition6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, let the CDF of the event time for the <math id="Thmproposition6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th position be given by the Kumaraswamy distribution with parameters <math id="Thmproposition6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmproposition6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b^{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., <math id="Thmproposition6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{T^{i}}(t)=1-(1-t^{a})^{b^{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{T^{i}}(t)=1-(1-t^{a})^{b^{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>, then the probability of an order <math id="Thmproposition6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is given by:</span></p>

<div id="A4.SS5.SSS4.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS5.SSS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">The proof is straightforward and follows directly from the following two results.</span></p>
<ol id="A4.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the event times <math id="A4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> are independent and have exponential distribution with parameter <math id="A4.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b^{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, then the probability of an order <math id="A4.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is given by:</p>

<tbody id="A4.Ex80"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex80.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle{\mathbb{P}}(\pi)=\prod_{i=1}^{L}\frac{b^{\pi(i)}}{\sum_{j=i}^{L}b^{\pi(j)}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle{\mathbb{P}}(\pi)=\prod_{i=1}^{L}\frac{b^{\pi(i)}}{\sum_{j=i}^{L}b^{\pi(j)}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> be a nonhomogeneous Poisson process with hazard rate of the form <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda(t)=b\beta(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(t)=b\beta(t)</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{N}_{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>N</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>u</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{N}_{u}</annotation></semantics></math> is a homogeneous Poisson process with warped time <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u=\int_{0}^{t}\beta(s)\mathrm{d}s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u=\int_{0}^{t}\beta(s)\mathrm{d}s</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{1}=\inf\{u:\bar{N}_{u}=1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">inf</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>N</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{1}=\inf\{u:\bar{N}_{u}=1\}</annotation></semantics></math>, be the first arrival time of the homogeneous Poisson process.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>

<section id="A4.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.6 </span>Sampling</h3>

<div id="A4.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The generator network predicts learnable hazard rates <math id="A4.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}},t}^{\theta,i}(x_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mtext encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}},t}^{\theta,i}(x_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> for insertion at gap position <math id="A4.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}},t}^{\theta,i}(x_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}},t}^{\theta,i}(x_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> for unmasking at masked position <math id="A4.SS6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, along with the token distribution <math id="A4.SS6.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="K^{\theta,i}(\cdot|x_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>K</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" </div>
<div id="A4.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We use a simple <math id="A4.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-leaping sampler that allows for larger time steps by sampling the number of events (insertions/unmaskings) in each interval <math id="A4.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[t_{n},t_{n+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[t_{n},t_{n+1})</annotation></semantics></math> from a Poisson distribution. For small <math id="A4.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=t_{n+1}-t_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=t_{n+1}-t_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, the first-order approximation gives Poisson intensities <math id="A4.SS6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}\lambda_{s}\mathrm{d}s\approx\lambda_{t_{n}}\cdot\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}\lambda_{s}\mathrm{d}s\approx\lambda_{t_{n}}\cdot\tau</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>

<section id="A4.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.7 </span>Truncation vs Rescaling</h3>

<div id="A4.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We need to sample two event times <math id="A4.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}</annotation></semantics></math> with a constrant <math id="A4.SS7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}&lt;{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}&lt;{T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}</annotation></semantics></math>. For constructing a learnable schedule for this we need to parameterize</p>

<p id="A4.SS7.p1.2" class="ltx_p">It is straightforward to parameterize <math id="A4.SS7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{P}}({T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}\leq t)" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}(0)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}{\textnormal{in}}}}(0)=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" However, for <math id="A4.SS7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{P}}({T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}\leq t\mid{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}=s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#264690;" mathcolor="#264690">in</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{P}}({T_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}\leq t\mid{T_{\color[rgb]{0.1484,0.2734,0.5664}\textnormal{in}}}=s)</annotation></semantics></math>, we have two easy choices. We can take a base monotonic function <math id="A4.SS7.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> and either <span id="A4.SS7.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">truncate</span> or <span id="A4.SS7.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">rescale</span> it to <math id="A4.SS7.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[s,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[s,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, where,</p>

<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Details of the experiment setup</h2>

<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Graph Traversal</h3>

<section id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dataset.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the star graphs dataset from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Patel et al. (2025b)</a></cite> obtained from <a href="https://huggingface.co/collections/dhruveshpatel/insertion-based-generation" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Hugging Face Hub</a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Model.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following the setup in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al. (2025a)</a></cite>, we use a linear layer for modeling the insertion lengths in each gap for FlexMDM.
For LMFlexMDM, we use two MLP layers for modeling the parameters of the learned target rates.</p>
</div>
</section>

<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A6.T7" title='In Fixing target unmasking rate (𝑏_"um"=1) ‣ F.2.1 Examples: Generation Order ‣ F.2 Star Graph Traversal ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analyses ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics' class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> shows the results for <span id="A6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">de novo</span> small molecule generation with additional nucleus-sampling <math id="A6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> values, as well as a shared-backbone implemenetation.</p>

<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Flexibility <span id="A6.SS1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">vs</span> Stability</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A6.F9" title="In F.1 Flexibility vs Stability ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analyses ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows the loss comparison for the hard star graph traversal task with and without fixing target unmasking rate (<math id="A6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>). As seen, fixing the target unmasking rate stabilizes the training significantly, and as shown in <a href="#A6.T6" title="In F.2.1 Examples: Generation Order ‣ F.2 Star Graph Traversal ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analyses ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, it also improves the overall performance of the final generator.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F9" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18695v1/x1.svg" id="A6.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:286/175;" width="286" height="175"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A6.F9.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="A6.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Loss comparison for the hard star graph traversal task with and without fixing target unmasking rate (<math id="A6.F9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>). The erratic dynamics of a fully unconstrained set of target rates motivates freezing <math id="A6.F9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>

<section id="A6.SS2.SSS1.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Fixing target unmasking rate (<math id="A6.SS2.SSS1.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>)</h5>

<div id="A6.SS2.SSS1.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS1.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A6.F9" title="In F.1 Flexibility vs Stability ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analyses ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows the loss comparison for the hard star graph traversal task with and without fixing target unmasking rate (<math id="A6.SS2.SSS1.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">b</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#990000;" mathcolor="#990000">um</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}b_{{\color[rgb]{0.6016,0,0}\textnormal{um}}}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>). As seen, fixing the target unmasking rate stabilizes the training significantly, and as shown in <a href="#A6.T6" title="In F.2.1 Examples: Generation Order ‣ F.2 Star Graph Traversal ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analyses ‣ Insertion Based Sequence Generation with Learnable Order Dynamics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, it also improves the overall performance of the final generator.</p>
</div>
